title.en: Email and multimedia: SMTP, and lossy compression (R2 · 6, 7)
title.zh: 邮件与多媒体：SMTP 与有损压缩（复2 · 6、7）

description.en: How an email travels and what an SMTP conversation looks like, which gives its strength and its weakness; what lossy compression gives up and why multimedia needs it; then MIME, mailboxes and streaming.
description.zh: 一封邮件怎么走、一次 SMTP 对话长什么样，它的优点和缺点就在里面；有损压缩放弃了什么，多媒体为什么离不开它；再看 MIME、收信和流媒体。

name.en: Email architecture: user agents and mail transfer agents (MTA)
name.zh: 电子邮件的架构：用户代理与邮件传输代理 (email architecture, user agent, MTA)
邮件格式与 MIME (message format, MIME)
多媒体压缩：无损与有损 (compression, lossless vs lossy)
抖动与客户端缓冲 (jitter, playout buffer)

description.en: Thinking lossy compression just means lower quality, without saying the result is an approximation
description.zh: 以为有损压缩只是“质量更差”，没说出结果是对原数据的近似

paras.en: Name one advantage and one disadvantage of SMTP.
paras.zh: 说出 SMTP 的一个优点和一个缺点。

items.en: **SMTP** (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) carries email from your mail program to your mail server, and from mail server to mail server.
items.zh: **SMTP**（Simple Mail Transfer Protocol，简单邮件传输协议）把邮件从你的邮件程序送到你的邮件服务器，再在邮件服务器之间传送。

items.en: **One advantage and one disadvantage**: two items. Each is a property of the protocol, plus why it helps or hurts.
items.zh: **一个优点和一个缺点**：两项。每一项都是协议的一个特性，再加上它为什么有利或有害。

text.en: Both come straight out of what an SMTP conversation looks like, so that is where the lesson goes: how a message travels, and then one conversation, line by line.
text.zh: 两项都直接来自 SMTP 对话的样子，所以这一课就从这里走：先看一封邮件怎么走，再一行一行地看一次对话。

text.en: Email has two kinds of programs. **User agents** are what you read and write mail in (Outlook, the Mail app). **Message transfer agents** (MTAs), also called mail servers, move mail from the sender's side to the receiver's.
text.zh: 邮件系统里有两类程序。**用户代理**（user agent）是你读写邮件的程序（Outlook、手机上的邮件）。**邮件传输代理**（MTA，message transfer agent），也叫邮件服务器，负责把邮件从发件方送到收件方。

alt.en: Four boxes in a row: Alice's user agent, Alice's mail server, Bob's mail server, Bob's user agent. SMTP carries the message for submission and for transfer; IMAP or POP3 for final delivery.
alt.zh: 一排四个方框：Alice 的用户代理、Alice 的邮件服务器、Bob 的邮件服务器、Bob 的用户代理。提交和传送用 SMTP；最终投递用 IMAP 或 POP3。

caption.en: Submission (SMTP, port 587, with a password) and transfer between servers (SMTP, port 25); final delivery to Bob's program by IMAP or POP3.
caption.zh: 提交（SMTP，端口 587，需要密码）和服务器之间的传送（SMTP，端口 25）；最终投递到 Bob 的程序用 IMAP 或 POP3。

text.en: Why not SMTP all the way to Bob? SMTP *pushes* a message to a server that must be up to accept it. Bob's laptop is often off or asleep, so the message waits in his always-on mail server until his user agent *pulls* it with IMAP or POP3.
text.zh: 为什么不一路用 SMTP 送到 Bob 手里？SMTP 是把邮件*推*给一台必须在线才能接收的服务器。Bob 的笔记本常常关着或休眠，所以邮件先在他那台一直在线的邮件服务器里等着，直到他的用户代理用 IMAP 或 POP3 把它*拉*下来。

text.en: Here is Alice's server handing a message to Bob's, over a TCP connection to port 25. Lines from the client start with C:, from the server with S:.
text.zh: 下面是 Alice 的服务器通过一条到 25 端口的 TCP 连接，把一封邮件交给 Bob 的服务器。C: 开头的是客户端发的，S: 开头的是服务器发的。

blocks.code:
S: 220 mail.unimelb.edu.au ESMTP ready
C: HELO laptop.example.com
S: 250 Hello laptop.example.com
C: MAIL FROM:<alice@example.com>
S: 250 OK
C: RCPT TO:<bob@unimelb.edu.au>
S: 250 OK
C: DATA
S: 354 End data with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>
C: From: alice@example.com
C: To: bob@unimelb.edu.au
C: Subject: Exam
C:
C: See you at nine.
C: .
S: 250 OK: queued
C: QUIT
S: 221 Bye

text.en: Two things stand out, and they are the answer.
text.zh: 有两点很显眼，它们就是答案。

items.en: **Every line is plain ASCII text.** Commands are words (HELO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA, QUIT); replies are a three-digit code and a phrase. A person can read the exchange, type it by hand to test a server, and see at once where it went wrong. That makes SMTP easy to develop, test and debug, and easy to implement.
items.zh: **每一行都是纯 ASCII 文本。**命令是单词（HELO、MAIL FROM、RCPT TO、DATA、QUIT）；回复是一个三位数的代码加一句话。人能直接读懂整个过程，能手敲命令去测试一台服务器，出错时一眼看出错在哪。所以 SMTP 容易开发、测试、调试，也容易实现。

items.en: **The client waits for a reply after every command.** Greeting, sender, recipient, DATA, the message, QUIT: about six round trips for one email. Over a long-distance link, most of the time goes on waiting.
items.zh: **客户端每发一条命令都要等回复。**问候、发件人、收件人、DATA、正文、QUIT：一封邮件大约六个往返。在长距离的链路上，大部分时间都花在等待上。

text.en: A third property is in the course too: SMTP was designed for 7-bit ASCII text. Images, attachments and non-Latin text must first be encoded as ASCII (MIME, usually base64), which makes them about a third larger.
text.zh: 课上还讲了第三个特性：SMTP 是为 7 位 ASCII 文本设计的。图片、附件和非拉丁文字得先编码成 ASCII（MIME，通常是 base64），体积会大约增加三分之一。

title.zh: 复习课 (2) 第 6 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: Advantage: SMTP is a simple, text-based (ASCII) protocol. Its commands and replies are human-readable, so it is easy to implement, test and debug; one can even type the commands by hand.
paras.zh: 优点：SMTP 是一个简单的、基于文本（ASCII）的协议。它的命令和回复人都能读懂，因此容易实现、测试和调试；甚至可以手工敲命令。

paras.en: Disadvantage: it needs several back-and-forth command/response exchanges for every email (HELO, MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA, ...), each waiting for a reply, which adds round trips and delay. (Also accepted: it carries only 7-bit ASCII, so binary content needs MIME encoding such as base64, which enlarges messages.)
paras.zh: 缺点：每封邮件都需要多次一来一回的命令/响应交换（HELO、MAIL FROM、RCPT TO、DATA……），每次都要等回复，增加了往返次数和延迟。（也可以写：它只能传 7 位 ASCII，二进制内容需要 base64 这类 MIME 编码，邮件会变大。）

text.en: For each item, name the property and say why it is good or bad. *SMTP is simple* alone is half an answer; *simple and text-based, so easy to read, debug and implement* is a whole one.
text.zh: 每一项都要说出特性，并说明为什么好或不好。只写“SMTP 很简单”是半个答案；写“简单、基于文本，所以容易读、调试和实现”才是完整的。

paras.en: What is lossy compression? Why is it important for encoding multimedia data?
paras.zh: 什么是有损压缩？为什么它对多媒体数据的编码很重要？

items.en: **Compression** encodes data in fewer bits at the source; **decoding** at the destination turns it back into something usable.
items.zh: **压缩**是在发送端用更少的位来编码数据；在接收端**解码**，再把它还原成能用的样子。

items.en: **What is**: a definition. **Why is it important for multimedia**: the reason that applies to audio, images and video in particular.
items.zh: **什么是**：要一个定义。**为什么对多媒体重要**：要的是专门针对音频、图像和视频的理由。

text.en: **Lossless** compression gives back exactly the original when decoded (ZIP, PNG, FLAC). It works by finding structure in the data, such as repeats and patterns. For text, programs and spreadsheets nothing else will do: a single changed bit can break them.
text.zh: **无损**压缩解码后得到的和原来一模一样（ZIP、PNG、FLAC）。它靠找出数据里的结构来压缩，比如重复和规律。文本、程序、电子表格只能用它：改动一位就可能把它们弄坏。

text.en: **Lossy** compression gives back only an **approximation** of the original. The aim is to throw away what matters least. For multimedia that works remarkably well, for two reasons.
text.zh: **有损**压缩解码后只得到原数据的**近似**。目标是扔掉最不要紧的部分。对多媒体，这一招非常管用，原因有两个。

items.en: **Multimedia is huge.** CD-quality sound is 44,100 samples per second × 16 bits × 2 channels ≈ 1.4 Mbit/s. Uncompressed HD video is 1920 × 1080 pixels × 24 bits × 30 frames per second ≈ 1.5 Gbit/s, far more than a home connection carries. Lossless compression shrinks such data only about twofold.
items.zh: **多媒体数据量巨大。**CD 音质的声音是每秒 44,100 个采样 × 16 位 × 2 声道 ≈ 1.4 Mbit/s。不压缩的高清视频是 1920 × 1080 像素 × 24 位 × 每秒 30 帧 ≈ 1.5 Gbit/s，远超家庭网络能承载的。无损压缩只能把这类数据缩小两倍左右。

items.en: **People cannot perceive all of it.** **Perceptual encoding** exploits the limits of our eyes and ears: a quiet sound right next to a loud one of similar pitch is masked and can be dropped (MP3); fine detail in colour matters less than in brightness (JPEG); much of each video frame repeats the one before (H.264). Throw that away and the result looks and sounds almost the same.
items.zh: **人感知不到其中很多部分。****感知编码**（perceptual encoding）利用的是眼睛和耳朵的局限：一个响亮的声音旁边、音高相近的轻声会被掩盖，可以去掉（MP3）；颜色的细节没有亮度的细节那么重要（JPEG）；视频的每一帧大部分和上一帧重复（H.264）。把这些扔掉，看起来、听起来几乎一样。

text.en: That is the trade the course's slide names: accepting a small loss of information buys a large payoff in the compression ratio.
text.zh: 这就是课件里说的那笔交易：接受一点点信息损失，换来压缩比上的巨大收益。

prompt.en: Which of these must be compressed losslessly?
prompt.zh: 下面哪个必须用无损压缩？

label.en: A program you download and run
label.zh: 一个你下载来运行的程序
一首用来在线播放的歌

feedback.en: Lossy is fine: the parts dropped are ones the ear does not notice.
feedback.zh: 有损就可以：扔掉的是耳朵察觉不到的部分。

label.en: A photo on a web page

feedback.en: Lossy is fine, and usual (JPEG): small changes to pixels are invisible.
feedback.zh: 有损就可以，而且很常见（JPEG）：像素上的微小变化看不出来。

explain.en: A program must come back bit for bit: one changed byte can crash it. Sound and pictures only have to look and sound right to a person.
explain.zh: 程序必须一位不差地还原：改了一个字节就可能崩溃。声音和图片只要在人看来、听来是对的就行。

title.zh: 复习课 (2) 第 7 题 · 满分答案

paras.en: In a lossy compression system the decoded data is only an approximation of the original data, not an exact copy (unlike lossless compression, where the original is reconstructed exactly).
paras.zh: 在有损压缩系统里，解码得到的数据只是原数据的近似，而不是精确的副本（无损压缩则能精确还原原数据）。

paras.en: It is important for multimedia because audio, images and video are very large, and lossy systems based on perceptual encoding discard information that human eyes and ears barely notice. Accepting a small loss of information gives a much larger compression ratio (about 10 times for music, hundreds of times for video) than lossless methods can, which greatly reduces the bandwidth and storage multimedia needs.
paras.zh: 它对多媒体很重要，因为音频、图像和视频的数据量非常大，而基于感知编码的有损系统扔掉的是人眼和人耳几乎察觉不到的信息。接受一点信息损失，就能得到比无损方法大得多的压缩比（音乐约 10 倍，视频可达数百倍），大大降低多媒体所需的带宽和存储。

text.en: The definition earns its mark with the word *approximation*. The reason earns its marks with *perceptual* (what is dropped is what people do not notice) and *compression ratio* (what is gained).
text.zh: 定义那一分靠*近似*这个词。理由那几分靠*感知*（扔掉的是人察觉不到的）和*压缩比*（换来了什么）。

text.en: **MIME** (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) is how mail carries more than English text. It adds headers that say what the body is (`Content-Type: image/jpeg`) and how it was wrapped for the trip (`Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`), and lets one message hold several parts, such as text and an attachment. **Base64** turns every 3 bytes into 4 ASCII characters, so an attachment travels about 4/3 of its size.
text.zh: **MIME**（多用途互联网邮件扩展）让邮件能装下英文文本以外的东西。它加了一些头部，说明正文是什么（`Content-Type: image/jpeg`）、为了运送包装成了什么样（`Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64`），还让一封邮件可以由好几个部分组成，比如正文加一个附件。**Base64** 把每 3 个字节变成 4 个 ASCII 字符，所以附件在路上的大小约为原来的 4/3。

text.en: **Final delivery.** **POP3** downloads the mail to one device and, usually, removes it from the server. **IMAP** keeps the mail on the server, with folders, so several devices see the same mailbox. **Webmail** (Gmail) is a user agent made of web pages: your browser talks HTTP to the mail service, which still uses SMTP between mail servers.
text.zh: **最终投递。****POP3** 把邮件下载到一台设备上，通常还会从服务器上删掉。**IMAP** 把邮件留在服务器上，带文件夹，几台设备看到的是同一个邮箱。**网页邮箱**（比如 Gmail）是一个由网页组成的用户代理：浏览器和邮件服务之间说 HTTP，而邮件服务器之间仍然用 SMTP。

title.en: Streaming: jitter, buffers and lost packets
title.zh: 流媒体：抖动、缓冲和丢包

text.en: Packets of a stream do not arrive at an even pace: the delay varies from packet to packet. That variation is **jitter**. A player that played each packet the moment it arrived would stutter, so it first fills a **buffer** and plays from it at a steady pace. The trade-off, from the course: a **small buffer** starts quickly but stalls when jitter is large; a **large buffer** makes you wait at the start but rides out the jitter.
text.zh: 一个流里的包不是匀速到达的：每个包的延迟都不一样。这种变化叫**抖动**（jitter）。播放器要是包一到就播，就会一卡一卡的，所以它先攒满一个**缓冲区**，再从里面匀速播放。课上讲的取舍：**小缓冲区**开播快，但抖动大时会卡住；**大缓冲区**开头要等，但能扛住抖动。

text.en: Lost packets are handled without retransmission where time matters: **forward error correction** sends extra data, such as one parity packet (the XOR of four data packets) from which any one of the four can be rebuilt; **error concealment** at the receiver fills a gap, for example by interpolating between frames. A live call keeps its buffer small and skips late packets, which is why it runs over RTP and UDP.
text.zh: 在讲究时效的场合，丢包不靠重传来处理：**前向纠错**（FEC）多发一些数据，比如每四个数据包配一个校验包（四个包的异或），丢了其中任何一个都能恢复；接收方的**错误掩盖**（error concealment）把缺口补上，比如在前后两帧之间插值。实时通话的缓冲区很小，迟到的包直接跳过，所以它跑在 RTP 和 UDP 上。

title.en: Your turn: pushing and pulling mail

prompt.en: Why does Bob's user agent collect his mail with IMAP or POP3, rather than having it delivered to his laptop by SMTP?
prompt.zh: 为什么 Bob 的用户代理用 IMAP 或 POP3 来收信，而不是让邮件通过 SMTP 直接送到他的笔记本上？

label.en: SMTP pushes mail to a server that must be up to accept it, and Bob's laptop is often off
label.zh: SMTP 是把邮件推给一台必须在线才能接收的服务器，而 Bob 的笔记本常常关着

feedback.en: With MIME encoding it can; that is how every attachment travels between servers.
feedback.zh: 用 MIME 编码就能运；服务器之间的附件都是这么走的。

feedback.en: Speed is not the reason. The receiving end of SMTP has to be online when the mail is sent.
feedback.zh: 原因不在速度。SMTP 的接收端必须在发信的那一刻在线。

explain.en: Mail waits in Bob's always-on server; his user agent pulls it whenever he is online.
explain.zh: 邮件在 Bob 那台一直在线的服务器上等着；他的用户代理什么时候上线，什么时候拉下来。

title.en: Your turn: an attachment in transit

prompt.en: A 300 KB photo is attached to an email and encoded in base64. About how large is it in transit, in KB?
prompt.zh: 一封邮件附带一张 300 KB 的照片，用 base64 编码。它在路上大约多大，以 KB 计？

explain.en: Base64 turns every 3 bytes into 4 characters: $300 \times 4/3 = 400$ KB.
explain.zh: base64 把每 3 个字节变成 4 个字符：$300 \times 4/3 = 400$ KB。

title.en: Your turn: how much MP3 saves

prompt.en: CD-quality audio is 1411 kbit/s. Encoded as MP3 at 128 kbit/s, what is the compression ratio? (One decimal.)
prompt.zh: CD 音质的音频是 1411 kbit/s。编码成 128 kbit/s 的 MP3，压缩比是多少？（保留一位小数。）

explain.en: $1411 / 128 \approx 11.0$: the MP3 is about eleven times smaller, and most listeners cannot tell.
explain.zh: $1411 / 128 \approx 11.0$：MP3 小了大约十一倍，大多数听众听不出区别。

title.en: Your turn: why the player waits
title.zh: 你来：播放器为什么要等

prompt.en: Why does a video player wait a few seconds before it starts to play a stream?
prompt.zh: 为什么视频播放器在开始播放一个流之前要先等几秒？

key_points.en: To fill a buffer before playing
key_points.zh: 为了在播放前先填满缓冲区

key_points.en: Packets arrive with varying delay (jitter); the buffer absorbs it so playback stays smooth
key_points.zh: 包到达的延迟各不相同（抖动）；缓冲区把它吸收掉，播放才平稳

key_points.en: A larger buffer means a longer wait at the start but fewer stalls
key_points.zh: 缓冲区越大，开头等得越久，但卡顿越少

model_answer.en: It is filling a playout buffer. Packets arrive with varying delay (jitter), so playing each one as it arrives would stall whenever one is late; playing from a buffer at a steady pace hides the variation. The bigger the buffer, the longer the wait at the start but the fewer the stalls.
model_answer.zh: 它在填播放缓冲区。包到达的延迟时快时慢（抖动），要是来一个播一个，只要有一个迟到就会卡住；从缓冲区里匀速地播，就把这种变化藏起来了。缓冲区越大，开头等得越久，但卡顿越少。

explain.en: The buffer trades start-up delay for smoothness: that trade is what the question is after.
explain.zh: 缓冲区是用开播的延迟换平稳：题目要的就是这个取舍。
